originalProposals.reason: Factually inaccurate/oversimplified as stated. Wood-combustion/pyrolysis science shows heating wood to ~400°C completes pyrolysis into charcoal (still holding roughly 30% tar by weight) — not ash; full ashing requires further oxidation at roughly 500-600°C and beyond with sustained air exposure. Naming 400°C as the point where 'wood turns into ashes' conflates charring with full combustion to ash and would teach a specific, checkable, wrong figure to a child. Candidate G4-M-4 ('describe changes in properties of materials ... such as changes when wood or coal are burned') would otherwise be a clean two-facet match (burning; new-properties/ash-smoke), but the claim needs correction before placement. Potential destination: G4-M-4, once the temperature/ash claim is corrected (e.g., wood chars/forms charcoal at ~400°C; full ashing needs higher, sustained heat).
